home.whoWeAre: Agriculture People Poverty Line Coaching Education Society (APPLES) is a non-profit, non-political, secular and charitable organisation based on love and concern for the poor, vulnerable and marginalised. Registered in 1995 (Reg. No. 154) under the Societies Registration Act XXI of 1860, we work in rural villages and urban slums of Anantapuramu district.

about.intro: A community-centred society serving Anantapuramu district since 1995.
about.overview: APPLES is a non-profit, non-political, secular and charitable organisation based on love and concern for the poor, vulnerable and marginalised. It was registered on 31 January 1995 under the Societies Registration Act XXI of 1860 (Reg. No. 154). Our activities run in rural villages and urban slums of Anantapuramu district, funded by government grants and schemes and by contributions from individuals, companies, trusts and the general public.
about.inspiration: Mr. S. Thirupal founded APPLES in 1995 with a motto of social justice and community development, inspired by Sri S.R. Sankaran IAS, who dedicated his whole life to the welfare of poor, deprived and marginalised communities. As Principal Secretary for Social Welfare in Andhra Pradesh he set up the schools and hostels for Dalit children that grew into the AP Social Welfare Residential Schools.
about.vision: Economic, social and environmentally sustainable development among deprived and marginalised people, so they lead a life of dignity and quality by accessing the resources and services available to them.
about.mission: Improve the lives of women, children, youth and the farming community through education, health, economic empowerment and social amenities.
aims: Stimulate people's involvement and organise community action for social, economic and cultural development.
Improve the quality of life of the farming community by promoting sustainable agriculture.
Seek collaboration with other voluntary organisations and government agencies.
Educate women and youth on their rights for equal status in health, social, political and economic development.
Network with NGOs and government organisations working in the same field.

stories.intro: Real outcomes from our programmes in Anantapuramu district.

items.title: 48 elders back with their families
items.text: Through outreach, counselling and family tracing, nearly 48 abandoned elderly people have returned to family life.

items.title: 89 children receive special learning kits
items.text: A screening camp with NIPED Hyderabad assessed 124 children; 89 received educational kits for children with special needs.

items.title: 92 people reach mental health care
items.text: Awareness and referral work connected 92 people with mental health conditions and other health problems to government hospitals.

items.title: 92 women start their own livelihoods
items.text: With SERP-supported self-help groups and bank linkages, 92 women now run their own income-generating activities.

items.title: 54 members earning on their own
items.text: The Sustainable Livelihood Development Programme helped 54 members set up and manage their own livelihoods.

items.title: 640 farmers practise natural farming
items.text: In the Venkatapuram Cluster, 640 farmers are using Zero Budget Natural Farming methods with APPLES and RySS.
